title: Retention Controls Overview (v1)
author: Naomi Feldman
body:
## Purpose
This page provides a high-level overview of Redwood Inference retention controls (v1): what data types are covered, defaults and guardrails, differences across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments, legal hold semantics, and where to find technical details and runbooks.

This is the canonical reference for:
- Product + Sales/Solutions explanations of “what is configurable”
- Engineering alignment on “what is enforced” and “how we prove it”
- GRC alignment on baseline evidence and customer-facing attestations

---

## Scope (v1)
### In scope
Retention controls apply to the following categories (see “Supported data types” for details):
- Audit logs (security/admin audit events)
- Admin activity (Console and API configuration changes; overlaps with audit logging but called out for coverage)
- Inference request metadata (non-payload metadata; where available)
- Telemetry / analytics datasets (eligible tables only)
- Selected operational logs where applicable and supported by the backing system

Controls are exposed:
- In Console (tenant admins): view defaults, set policy within guardrails, view effective policy, view enforcement status, and view holds/exceptions.
- Via API (automation): read/write policy and read effective policy/enforcement status.

### Out of scope / later
- Customer-configurable retention for all raw inference payload content (prompt/response bodies), except where explicitly documented for a given product mode.
- Custom retention across every infrastructure log stream (some streams are governed by SRE standards or vendor-managed limits).

---

## Key concepts and definitions
**Tenant**: A customer account boundary used for configuration, isolation, and reporting.

**Data type**: A logical category of stored data subject to retention (e.g., audit logs vs telemetry tables). Policies are configured per data type.

**Retention duration**: The time window (e.g., 30 days) that data is retained before becoming eligible for deletion.

**Effective policy**: The resolved policy after applying precedence and guardrails across organization/tenant/environment/region (see “Policy model and precedence”).

**Enforcement**: The mechanism that makes data older than the retention duration eligible for deletion (e.g., TTL/partition expiration, scheduled deletion jobs, compaction). Enforcement is not “best effort”; it is monitored and auditable.

**Legal hold**: A flag that prevents deletion for a defined scope until released, overriding retention enforcement for the held scope.

---

## Supported data types (v1)
The table below summarizes what is covered in v1 and what is configurable.

| Data type | What it contains | Customer configurable? | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Audit logs | Security/admin audit events (who/what/when), including retention policy changes | Yes | Primary compliance artifact. Export behavior documented separately. |
| Admin activity | Admin actions in Console/API (often stored as audit events) | Yes (via Audit logs policy) | Treated as part of audit logging coverage for v1; may be presented as a filtered view. |
| Inference request metadata | Request IDs, timestamps, model ID/version, token counts, latency, status codes; excludes raw prompt/response bodies unless explicitly stated | Partially | Coverage depends on deployment mode and selected observability features. |
| Telemetry / analytics (eligible tables) | Aggregations and events used for dashboards, usage analytics, and reliability analysis | Yes (eligible tables only) | Some derived aggregates may have fixed retention; see exceptions. |
| Operational logs (selected) | Operational signals directly tied to tenant-facing features (e.g., enforcement worker logs/metrics) | No (v1) | Generally governed by SRE standards; retained for platform reliability; customer visibility is via dashboards and reports, not raw logs. |

Important: In v1, “retention controls” refers to **data Redwood stores as part of operating the service**. It does not change customer-controlled storage (e.g., customer SIEM, customer exports) once data has been exported.

---

## Deployment mode differences (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
Retention capabilities vary by product due to infrastructure and customer-managed controls.

### Hosted API (Redwood-hosted multi-tenant)
Supported:
- Tenant-configurable retention for audit logs
- Tenant-configurable retention for eligible telemetry/analytics datasets
- Limited/partial retention controls for inference request metadata (metadata only)

Notes:
- Defaults are set by Redwood; customers may decrease/increase within guardrails.
- Enforcement is performed in Redwood-managed storage systems with monitoring/alerts.

### Dedicated (reserved capacity, isolated compute; Redwood-managed control plane)
Supported:
- Same as Hosted for audit logs and eligible telemetry/analytics datasets
- Additional isolation and potentially broader metadata retention options depending on configuration

Notes:
- Dedicated may support longer maximum retention for select data types, subject to contract and storage implications.

### Private (VPC / on-prem)
Supported:
- Audit log retention controls supported when the Private control plane is deployed with the v1 retention services enabled
- Telemetry/analytics retention depends on which components are enabled (some customers disable analytics pipelines)

Notes:
- In Private deployments, **customer-owned infrastructure may enforce additional retention at the storage layer**. Redwood policy applies within the Redwood components we run, but cannot override customer-managed storage policies.
- Where customers bring their own logging/observability stack, Redwood will provide configuration guidance and “expected behavior” targets.

---

## Default retention policies (v1)
Defaults are designed to be compliant-friendly while minimizing unnecessary storage.

### Default values
Unless otherwise contracted, Redwood defaults are:

| Data type | Default retention | Rationale |
|---|---:|---|
| Audit logs | 365 days | Common enterprise expectation for security auditability. |
| Inference request metadata (where applicable) | 30 days | Supports troubleshooting and performance analysis without long-term metadata accumulation. |
| Telemetry/analytics (eligible tables) | 90 days | Supports trend analysis and product analytics while limiting footprint. |

### Customer tiers / contracts
Some enterprise contracts may specify different defaults (e.g., 90/365/730 days for audit logs). Where contract terms differ, the contract governs and the configured guardrails should reflect the contracted maximums.

---

## Guardrails (min/max) and safety constraints
Retention controls are configurable, but bounded.

### Guardrails (v1 standard)
Guardrails are enforced at policy validation time (Console/API) and reflected in the effective policy.

| Data type | Minimum retention | Maximum retention | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Audit logs | 90 days | 730 days | “Never delete” is not permitted in v1. Exceptions require Legal + Security approval and are implemented as legal holds, not infinite retention. |
| Inference request metadata (where applicable) | 7 days | 90 days | “0 days” is not supported; disabling storage is handled via separate data handling controls (out of scope for v1). |
| Telemetry/analytics (eligible tables) | 30 days | 365 days | Some tables are fixed retention (non-eligible); those are clearly labeled in Console. |

### Additional constraints
- **Legal hold overrides retention** for the held scope.
- **Deletion is asynchronous**: after the retention duration, data becomes eligible for deletion and is removed on the next enforcement cycle (see “Enforcement and auditability”).
- **Regional constraints**: policies may be applied per region/environment; some datasets are region-bound by design and cannot be moved cross-region to satisfy retention.

---

## Legal hold semantics (v1)
Legal holds are intended for litigation/regulatory preservation and are treated as a higher-priority override than retention.

### What a legal hold does
- Prevents deletion of held data beyond the configured retention duration.
- Applies to a defined scope (tenant + data types; optionally region and date range where supported).
- Is auditable: creation, updates, and release are recorded as audit events.

### What a legal hold does NOT do
- It does not automatically export data; it only preserves data in place.
- It does not override data that has already been deleted prior to the hold.

### Who can place a legal hold
- Redwood internal: Security Engineering + Legal Counsel (per process).
- Customer: customers request a hold via support/CSM; customers cannot self-serve legal holds in v1.

### Releasing a legal hold
- Requires approval per the “Retention Exceptions & Legal Holds” process.
- On release, normal retention enforcement resumes (data older than the configured retention may be deleted in subsequent enforcement cycles).

Link: /security-and-compliance/risk-and-exceptions/retention-exceptions-and-legal-holds-process

---

## Policy model and precedence (high level)
Retention policy evaluation follows deterministic precedence rules so customers can understand what will happen.

At a high level:
1) Legal hold (highest priority)
2) Explicit tenant policy (if set)
3) Environment/region overrides (if applicable)
4) Redwood defaults
5) Guardrails applied (min/max clamping and disallowed values)

Console always shows:
- Configured policy (what the admin set)
- Effective policy (what will be enforced)
- Reason/explanation when a value is clamped or overridden

Technical details and examples:
- /security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/retention-policy-schema-and-evaluation

---

## Enforcement and auditability (high level)
### Enforcement approach
Retention is enforced using a hybrid model (TTL where supported + scheduled deletion jobs where required) to meet auditability and datastore constraints.

What customers and auditors should expect:
- Data older than the effective retention is targeted by enforcement mechanisms.
- Enforcement runs on a schedule with backpressure and safety limits to prevent platform impact.
- Enforcement is monitored, with alerts on lag/backlog/error rate.

ADR (design rationale and trade-offs):
- /architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-retention-enforcement-strategy

### Auditability and evidence
We maintain evidence that retention is:
- Configured (policy records + admin audit events)
- Enforced (job runs, metrics, deletion counters, TTL settings)
- Monitored (dashboards + alerts)

Customer-facing artifacts are bundled in the Compliance Reporting Pack (v1):
- /security-and-compliance/compliance-evidence/compliance-reporting-pack-v1

Control mapping (SOC2/ISO-aligned):
- /security-and-compliance/compliance-evidence/control-mapping-retention-and-audit-logging

---

## Audit log exports and retention interaction
Audit log exports (manual export and SIEM integration where supported) are designed to respect retention boundaries.

Key points:
- Exports include only data still retained at export time (subject to retention + legal hold).
- Exports include metadata/warnings where retention boundaries may affect completeness (e.g., “export window exceeds retained window”).
- For Private deployments, exports may depend on customer-managed connectors.

Details:
- /security-and-compliance/audit-logging/audit-log-retention-and-exports

---

## Console and API surfaces (what customers see)
### Console (Retention Controls)
Console provides:
- Retention settings per supported data type
- Effective policy view with explanations
- Enforcement status panel (last run time, last successful run, current lag where available)
- Legal hold banner (when a hold applies) and link to support process
- Change history (via audit logs)

### API
API supports:
- Read/write retention policy (tenant-scoped)
- Read effective policy
- Read enforcement status

Notes:
- Policy write requires appropriate admin permissions.
- All policy changes generate audit events.

(Implementation details live in the policy schema + evaluation doc.)

## Known limitations (v1)
- Not all operational logs are customer-configurable; many are governed centrally for reliability and security.
- Some analytics datasets are not eligible for tenant-configurable retention (fixed retention); Console will label these.
- Private deployments may have partial functionality depending on enabled components and customer-managed storage.

---

## Frequently asked questions
### Can we set retention to “never delete”?
Not in v1. “Never delete” is disallowed by policy validation. If there is a legal requirement, use the legal hold process (Security + Legal approval) for a scoped preservation.

### Does retention delete data immediately at N days?
No. Data becomes eligible for deletion after the retention window and is removed on the next enforcement cycle. Console provides enforcement status and last run information.

### Are prompt/response bodies covered?
In v1, customer-configurable retention for raw inference payload content is out of scope (unless a specific deployment feature explicitly documents payload storage and retention). v1 focuses on audit logs, admin/audit events, eligible telemetry/analytics, and metadata.

### What evidence can Redwood provide in a security review?
The Compliance Reporting Pack (v1) includes a retention attestation, audit log coverage summary, and a control-to-evidence matrix with verification steps.
